label: fw.wad, the mod's textures, judged as one set: a concrete wall, a wet concrete floor, a steel grate with holes, a catwalk floor, a pipe-covered wall, a hazard-striped trim, a rusted steel plate, a control panel with dials, a sodium lamp's face (lit), the water, a sign reading PUMP 3, a door

T1.reason: All twelve textures (fw_plain0 to fw_plain11) are one flat mid-grey with nothing drawn on them. None reads as a concrete wall, wet floor, grate, catwalk, pipe wall, hazard trim, rusted plate, control panel, lamp face, water, PUMP 3 sign or door. A player could not name the material or purpose of any of them.

T2.reason: Every texture is the same neutral grey. The brief asks for yellow hazard paint, rust brown, a sodium-orange lamp face, green-grey water and a red or steel door. Grey is plausible only for the concrete, so most of the set is far off the colours the brief gives.

T3.reason: There is no pattern at all: no panels, seams, grate holes, catwalk treads, pipes, stripes, dials or lettering. Nothing has a scale to compare against a Half-Life wall.

T4.reason: A flat colour has no seam where it repeats, so the edge-step measurement would pass trivially. I score it lower than the measurement allows because there is no content that tiles, which makes the seamlessness meaningless.

T5.reason: Measured detail is 0 for all twelve, far below Half-Life's band (lower quartile 19.7, median 30.1, upper quartile 45). Flat and on a wall, these are blank fills and nowhere near as detailed or believable as the game's own textures.

T6.reason: The sizes (64x64) are valid, but no name carries the meaning the brief requires. The water is not a '!' liquid texture, the grate is not a '{' texture with transparent holes, and the sodium lamp face is not lit (no light-emitting texture). Each is fw_plainN in a single colour.
